newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt airport wins Delta handling deal.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt airport wins Delta handling deal.

text.p: Flughafen Frankfurt Main AG (FAG) said it has signed an agreement with Delta Air Lines to take over handling of the carrier's aircraft and freight from June 1.
Under the deal, FAG will take on 92 Delta staff for aircraft handling and a further 60 for airfreight handling in the newly-opened FAG cargo terminal at Frankfurt airport.
A further 29 Delta staff will be employed by cabin cleaning firm Airport Services GmbH, in which FAG has a 50 percent stake.

The airport authority gave no value for the contract, which was signed after weeks of negotiations and followed Delta's decision to drop eight of its 14 weekly Frankfurt flights from June with up to 440 job losses.
This decision prompted five staff to go on an 11-day hunger strike until a redundancy package was agreed between airline and the OeTV union in early April.
Delta will continue to be responsible for passenger check-in for its six daily flights in Frankfurt airport Terminal 2.
FAG said it won the Delta contract in the face of strong competition from other handling companies at Frankfurt airport.
Chairman Wilhelm Bender said: "The Delta decision clearly confirms FAG's success in transforming itself into a highly competitive and market-orientated company."
